---
title: "K-means clustering"
execute:
  cache: false
---

We now fit centroids to the [speaker-relative Peterson-Barney representation](distance-and-scaling.qmd). Intended-vowel labels do not enter the fit. We fix $K=10$ only to compare a ten-centroid acoustic partition with the experiment's ten elicitation categories after fitting; this is not a claim that K-means discovered the category count.

## Reconstructing the feature matrix

```{r}
source_environment <- new.env(parent = emptyenv())
utils::data("pb52", package = "phonTools", envir = source_environment)
pb52 <- source_environment$pb52

stopifnot(
  identical(dim(pb52), c(1520L, 9L)),
  length(unique(pb52$speaker)) == 76L,
  all(table(pb52$speaker) == 20L)
)

vowels <- pb52 |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    row_id = dplyr::row_number(),
    token_id = sprintf(
      "speaker-%02d-%s-repetition-%d", speaker, vowel, repetition
    )
  ) |>
  dplyr::group_by(speaker) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    z_f1 = (f1 - mean(f1)) / stats::sd(f1),
    z_f2 = (f2 - mean(f2)) / stats::sd(f2)
  ) |>
  dplyr::ungroup()

X <- as.matrix(vowels[, c("z_f1", "z_f2")])
stopifnot(
  max(abs(tapply(vowels$z_f1, vowels$speaker, mean))) < 1e-12,
  max(abs(tapply(vowels$z_f2, vowels$speaker, mean))) < 1e-12
)
```

## Assignments, centroids, and loss

Let $\mathbf{x}_i\in\mathbb{R}^p$ be token $i$'s feature vector. For $K$ clusters, let

$$
z_i\in\{1,\ldots,K\}
$$

be its hard assignment and let

$$
\boldsymbol{\mu}_k\in\mathbb{R}^p
$$

be centroid $k$. [**K-means clustering**](https://online.stat.psu.edu/stat505/Lesson14) minimizes the within-cluster sum of squares

$$
W
=
\sum_{i=1}^{N}
\left\lVert
\mathbf{x}_i-\boldsymbol{\mu}_{z_i}
\right\rVert^2.
$$

For fixed centroids, the assignment step chooses

$$
z_i
=
\underset{k\in\{1,\ldots,K\}}{\operatorname{argmin}}
\left\lVert
\mathbf{x}_i-\boldsymbol{\mu}_k
\right\rVert^2.
$$

For fixed assignments, the update step replaces each centroid with the mean of its assigned rows:

$$
\boldsymbol{\mu}_k
=
\frac{1}{|C_k|}
\sum_{i\in C_k}\mathbf{x}_i.
$$

## Why the update is a mean

For one coordinate of one fixed cluster, the squared loss around a proposed center $\mu$ is

$$
Q(\mu)
=
\sum_{i=1}^{n}(x_i-\mu)^2.
$$

Its derivative is

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}Q}{\mathrm{d}\mu}
=
-2\sum_{i=1}^{n}(x_i-\mu).
$$

Setting this derivative to zero gives

$$
\sum_{i=1}^{n}x_i-n\mu=0,
$$

and thus

$$
\mu
=
\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n}x_i.
$$

The coordinatewise mean thus minimizes squared distance for fixed assignments.

## Fitting ten centroids

```{r}
seed <- 1952L
components <- 10L

set.seed(seed)
fit_k10 <- stats::kmeans(
  X,
  centers = components,
  nstart = 100L,
  iter.max = 200L,
  algorithm = "Hartigan-Wong"
)

fit_summary <- data.frame(
  quantity = c("centroids", "iterations", "within-cluster sum of squares"),
  value = c(components, fit_k10$iter, fit_k10$tot.withinss)
)
knitr::kable(fit_summary, digits = 3)
```

The fitted loss is `r round(fit_k10$tot.withinss, 3)`. The seed and 100 starts make this calculation reproducible and reduce sensitivity to one initialization. They do not establish a global optimum.

## Inspecting one observed assignment

The token used on the scaling page is row `r which.min(rowSums(sweep(X, 2, colMeans(X), "-")^2))`. We calculate its squared distance to every fitted centroid rather than inserting a constructed coordinate pair.

```{r}
pairwise_squared_distance <- function(x, centers) {
  x2 <- rowSums(x^2)
  c2 <- rowSums(centers^2)
  pmax(outer(x2, c2, "+") - 2 * tcrossprod(x, centers), 0)
}

reference_row <- which.min(rowSums(sweep(X, 2, colMeans(X), "-")^2))
reference_distances <- data.frame(
  cluster = seq_len(components),
  squared_distance = as.numeric(pairwise_squared_distance(
    X[reference_row, , drop = FALSE],
    fit_k10$centers
  ))
) |>
  dplyr::arrange(squared_distance) |>
  dplyr::mutate(distance_rank = dplyr::row_number())

stopifnot(reference_distances$cluster[1] == fit_k10$cluster[reference_row])
knitr::kable(reference_distances, digits = 3)
```

The nearest fitted centroid is cluster `r reference_distances$cluster[1]`, with squared distance `r round(reference_distances$squared_distance[1], 3)`. The integer label is arbitrary; its location and assigned observations define the fitted region.

## Verifying the update step on the fitted data

```{r}
centroid_check <- vowels |>
  dplyr::mutate(cluster = fit_k10$cluster) |>
  dplyr::group_by(cluster) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    assigned_tokens = dplyr::n(),
    observed_mean_z_f1 = mean(z_f1),
    observed_mean_z_f2 = mean(z_f2),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    fitted_z_f1 = fit_k10$centers[cluster, 1],
    fitted_z_f2 = fit_k10$centers[cluster, 2],
    maximum_absolute_difference = pmax(
      abs(observed_mean_z_f1 - fitted_z_f1),
      abs(observed_mean_z_f2 - fitted_z_f2)
    )
  )

stopifnot(max(centroid_check$maximum_absolute_difference) < 1e-12)
knitr::kable(centroid_check, digits = 3)
```

The fitted centroids equal the coordinatewise means of their assigned Peterson-Barney tokens to numerical tolerance. This observed check instantiates the update equation above.

```{r}
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-height: 4.5
#| fig-alt: "Within-speaker standardized Peterson and Barney vowel tokens colored by ten fitted K-means clusters, with centroid locations marked by black crosses."

plot_data <- vowels |>
  dplyr::mutate(cluster = factor(fit_k10$cluster))
centroids <- data.frame(
  cluster = factor(seq_len(components)),
  z_f1 = fit_k10$centers[, 1],
  z_f2 = fit_k10$centers[, 2]
)

ggplot2::ggplot(plot_data, ggplot2::aes(
  x = z_f2, y = z_f1, color = cluster
)) +
  ggplot2::geom_point(alpha = 0.48, size = 0.65) + # dqr-allow: algorithm-setting
  ggplot2::geom_point(
    data = centroids,
    ggplot2::aes(x = z_f2, y = z_f1),
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    color = "black",
    shape = 4,
    stroke = 1,
    size = 2.3
  ) +
  ggplot2::scale_x_reverse() +
  ggplot2::scale_y_reverse() +
  ggplot2::scale_color_viridis_d(option = "D", end = 0.9) +
  ggplot2::labs(
    x = "Within-speaker standardized F2",
    y = "Within-speaker standardized F1"
  ) +
  ggplot2::theme_classic(base_size = 11) +
  ggplot2::theme(legend.position = "none")
```

## Comparing with labels only after fitting

```{r}
external_ari <- mclust::adjustedRandIndex(fit_k10$cluster, vowels$vowel)
```

The adjusted Rand index (ARI) against the withheld intended-vowel metadata is `r round(external_ari, 3)`. This number measures alignment between two partitions after the acoustic fit. It does not turn a centroid into a vowel, establish perceptual validity, or make the analysis supervised.

## Alternation and local solutions

Each assignment step cannot increase $W$ because every token chooses its nearest current centroid. Each update step cannot increase $W$ because each centroid becomes the mean of its assigned rows. The procedure thus decreases or preserves the objective until it reaches a local solution.

K-means favors compact regions under squared Euclidean distance and assigns every token to exactly one region. Overlapping productions may not have that structure. A poor fit would diagnose this representation and objective, not the absence of organization in the production data.

## Checking the alternating updates

1. Which centroid receives the reference token, and what squared distance supports that assignment?
2. How does `centroid_check` verify the update equation?
3. Why can several starts improve the fitted loss without guaranteeing a global minimum?
4. Why was $K=10$ fixed before the intended-vowel comparison?
5. What does the post-fit ARI establish, and what does it leave open?

K-means alternates nearest-centroid assignments with mean updates in the declared acoustic geometry. The [next page](within-cluster-loss.qmd) shows how the fitted compactness changes when the number of centroids changes.
